title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 139 (Discharge of surety by creditor's act or omission impairing surety's eventual remedy)

content.overview: Section 139 provides that if the creditor does any act which is inconsistent with the rights of the surety, or omits to do any act which his duty to the surety requires him to do, and the eventual remedy of the surety himself against the principal debtor is thereby impaired, the surety is discharged.
content.glance: Creditor's act or omission that impairs the surety's eventual remedy against the principal debtor discharges the surety.
content.study: If the creditor does any act which is inconsistent with the rights of the surety, or omits to do any act which his duty to the surety requires him to do, and the eventual remedy of the surety himself against the principal debtor is thereby impaired, the surety is discharged. Current-law framing: the impairment of the surety's remedy is the key.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: If the creditor does any act which is inconsistent with the rights of the surety, or omits to do any act which his duty to the surety requires him to do, and the eventual remedy of the surety himself against the principal debtor is thereby impaired, the surety is discharged.

examples.title: Loss of security
examples.body: Creditor, without surety's consent, parts with a security held against the principal debtor, impairing the surety's eventual remedy. Surety is discharged to that extent.

hypotheticals.question: The creditor releases a security without the surety's consent, impairing the surety's remedy. Is the surety discharged?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes, under Section 139, if the eventual remedy is thereby impaired.
